why: Exactly k = at most k minus at most k-1: counting windows with exactly k odd numbers directly is awkward because a window can be shrunk past even numbers without changing its count. Counting windows with AT MOST k odd numbers is a plain sliding window (each right end adds right - left + 1), so subtract the two counts.
hints: Counting subarrays with at most k odd values is easier than exactly k. Why?
For at most k, each right end has a single smallest valid left, and every start from left to right works: add right - left + 1.
exactly(k) = atMost(k) - atMost(k - 1), with atMost(-1) = 0. Each atMost is one O(n) pass. (Prefix counts of odd numbers plus a hash map give the same answer.)
pitfalls: Negative numbers can be odd: use x % 2 != 0 (Python) or x & 1, not x % 2 == 1 in languages where -3 % 2 is -1.
k = 0 counts subarrays of only even numbers.
